definitions.explanation: The week after this one; the coming week. Used to refer to future events or plans in the week that follows the current one.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}{仕事|しごと}があります。
{来週|らいしゅう}の{月曜日|げつようび}に{会|あ}いましょう。
{来週|らいしゅう}までに{宿題|しゅくだい}を{出|だ}してください。
examples.english: Please submit the homework by next week.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}の{木曜日|もくようび}に{大切|たいせつ}な{会議|かいぎ}があるので、{準備|じゅんび}しています。
examples.english: There's an important meeting next Thursday, so I'm preparing for it.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}は{毎日|まいにち}{予定|よてい}があって{大変|たいへん}ですが、{週末|しゅうまつ}は{休|やす}めるので、{頑張|がんば}ります。
examples.english: I have plans every day next week and it'll be tough, but I can rest on the weekend so I'll do my best.

notes: Part of a time reference series: {先週|せんしゅう} (last week), {今週|こんしゅう} (this week), {来週|らいしゅう} (next week). The {来|らい} prefix means 'coming' or 'next' and also appears in {来月|らいげつ} (next month) and {来年|らいねん} (next year).
